free_tier.stated: Free of charge as long as the Inference API remains in experimental status; the experiment ends on 8 December 2026. Two open-weight models, Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 and Qwen3.8-27B, each with 262,144 tokens of context and text plus image input. Hetzner says it will email users before the experimental status changes.
free_tier.notes: The free unit is usage without a token allowance: there is no published credit or byte cap, only per-key rate limits. Usage timestamps and token counts are tracked; request and response content is not stored. The service is offered as is with no availability guarantee and the model list changes during the experiment; GET /v1/models is definitive. models.dev records 2 models at base https://inference.hetzner.com/v1.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a model request, not a stored object; the API stores no request or response content for the caller

retention.stated: not applicable: the API keeps only usage metadata (request timestamps, token counts) and states it does not store request or response content

egress.terms: The generated response is the payload; no separate egress allowance, quota or price is published for the Inference API.

interface_detail: OpenAI-compatible REST API with three endpoints: /v1/models, /v1/completions and /v1/chat/completions at https://inference.hetzner.com/v1, usable with any OpenAI-compatible SDK or HTTP client.
tooling: Any OpenAI Python or JavaScript SDK pointed at the base URL with a bearer token; the request examples are plain curl and the openai pip package.
chaining: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint with no per-token charge while the experiment runs can back agent stacks that already speak the OpenAI API, but the 10-requests-per-60-second ceiling and the 8 December 2026 end date make it a temporary bench rather than a durable dependency; durable state needs a separate storage record.

limits.value: per API key: 10 requests per 60 s, 4M input tokens per 60 s and 100k output tokens per 60 s; exceeding any limit returns HTTP 429

limits_note: Only a selected list of models is exposed and it changes during the experimental phase; the selection is not a guarantee. A bearer token is required on every request.
binding_note: With no charge or token cap, the first limit a caller meets is the 10-requests-per-60-second per-key ceiling, well before the 4M input or 100k output token ceilings.

identity_cost.detail: A bearer token is minted after login to a Hetzner account at experiments.hetzner.com. Account registration requires a valid email address, personal or business contact information and a billing address, with a phone number optional for advanced verification, and the email address must be verified by a link. Whether a card or ID check is required before a token can be created is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Experimental service offered as is: performance and availability are not guaranteed during high demand, no backups are created, the model list changes during the experiment, and the experiment ends on 8 December 2026.
confidence_note: The free status, end date, endpoints, models, rate limits and retention posture are quoted from Hetzner's own experimental Inference API documentation read on 2026-11-24; the account fields are quoted from Hetzner's account-getting-started page and the model count and base from models.dev the same day. The token-creation gate beyond login is unverified behind a sign-up.

notes: A free, token-unmetered OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint that runs only until 8 December 2026. Two Qwen models are exposed with text and image input. A Hetzner account and bearer token are needed, so it is not anonymous; the first binding constraint is the 10-requests-per-60-seconds per-key limit. Paid Hetzner cloud servers and the separately catalogued Storage Box and Object Storage offers are different products.
